t1.text: Roth Catha: from a flat lane to a turning wheel

s1.text:
What the current build does (seen running locally)

• The default view in drafting and play is a straight two-row lane; the wheel is behind a 'Whole wheel' toggle, so the round board never feels round.
• The whole wheel lays twelve equal cards on a ring: quadrants, owners, the ford and the direction of turn aren't visible.
• The phase line says 'Playing turn · step 1' but not how many steps remain, what comes next, or which duel this spot feeds.
• Actions are a bare list ('Turn Culann's hound', 'Hold') with no effect shown until after you commit; outcomes land only in the Moves log.
• The page header and long lede stay on screen during a match; hand and omens sit below the fold, far from the board.
• '6 in hand' sits above four card backs that are actually face-down omens.

s2.text:
Quality-of-life list (smaller, independent)

• Collapse the page header to a 56px bar during a match.
• Keep the hand docked under the wheel; tap a hand card to light up where it can go.
• Hover a geis or oath → its forbidden supports dim on the wheel.
• Show the keyboard keys already in the code (1–9, Enter, Esc, arrows) as small key caps.
• Label the enemy zone '6 in hand · 4 omens face down'.
• 'Replay the computer's move' button: step the last reply on the board.
• Animation speed: Off / Brisk / Ceremonial.
• The Moves log lines link to the spot they touched.

t2.text: Phone: the wheel as a dial, not a shrunken circle

s3.text:
One wheel, three zooms

• Desktop, 1100px and wider: the whole wheel in the middle (board 1), forecast on the left, actions on the right.
• Tablet, 700–1100px: the whole wheel at full width; forecast and actions in a two-tab panel under it; hand as a drawer.
• Phone, under 700px: the dial (board 5). We zoom so far into the wheel that only the arc in front of you shows, about three cards, with the front card full size. Swiping turns the wheel to look at other cards; the cards stay upright and only their places move, the neighbours sitting up-left and up-right of the front card; it snaps back to the front when you act.

Why it works where the small wheel didn't: the wheel is always round and always turning, but at phone size it never has to show 12 readable cards at once. The whole board is a map in the hub (tap it for board 6). You read a card by selecting it, not by squinting at it.

The current lane (FordLane.tsx) and the zoom in Wheel.tsx with its rotate-to-front code are already halfway there: the dial is the zoom with a bigger radius, the arc kept, and the hub turned into the map.

t3.text: The duel: champions and the Slúagh

s4.text:
The Slúagh and champions everywhere

Slúagh hosts
• A host is one fighter made of a host card and 2–3 monsters. On the wheel it is one hero spot with stacked edges and the combined numbers; tap it to see who rides with it.
• While drafting, choosing the monsters is part of placing the host, with live totals (board 7), not a row of buttons listing combinations.
• The Muster counts hosts as heroes and shows 'monsters to ride with them: n'.
• Their powers (Spirit blows can't be Blocked; they heal 2 when you rest) show on the fighter and as warnings on the actions they affect.

Champions
• They wait on a bench beside the hand, labelled with the duels you may call them in (the first player either duel, the second player only the second).
• Called in, the champion's card sits over the hero's on the wheel, with the hero showing beneath. The rule 'if he falls, your hero falls' stays visible on it.
• Geasa and oaths show as 'doesn't bind Lóegaire'.

t4.text: Settings: where the duels are fought

s5.text:
Settings: what the design assumes, and what to check

• The second player chooses between two places: the ford (neutral) or their own deck's home. engine/settings.ts currently lets them pick any of the eight; the screen assumes the two-way choice you described.
• It comes right after the decks and before the Muster, so both players sort their decks knowing the ground. A new 'Setting' step in the progress track (board 2).
• Shown wherever it changes a number: named in the match bar and duel header, +1/−1 badges on the supports it changes, a line in every preview and log sum (board 8), and the ford line and hub take on its look.
• The engine's own judgement of which setting suits a deck (fit() in settings.ts) can mark the stronger pick and list both sides' affected cards.

From the six starter decks:
• Clear homes: Ulster–Emain Macha, Sídhe–Brú na Bóinne, Merrow–the loughs, Slúagh–the western crossing.
• Connacht: Cruachan by name, but the Bog of Allen helps more of its supports.
• Fomóire: Conand's tower helps none of its supports; the computer takes the Fomóire to the loughs or the bog instead.
• Which deck is the Bog of Allen's home, if any?
